problem:
Construct the matrix $T$ of the linear transformation $T$ that acts on a vector in ${R}^{2}$ as follows (in the order given):

- It rotates the vector by $\frac{3\pi }{2}$ radians **counterclockwise** about the origin, then

- stretches the result by a scale factor of $6$ parallel to the $x$-axis, and finally

- reflects the result about the line $y=-x.$

|  |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $T=\,\,$ |  |  |  |  |
|  |  | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} |  |
worked_solution:
Let $P$ be the matrix that represents the rotation, $Q$ be the matrix that represents the stretching, and $R$ be the matrix that represents the reflection. These are given by the following elementary transformation matrices:

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,Q=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,R=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\,\,
$$

Hence, the combined transformation can be represented by the matrix $RQP:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =RQP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -6 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
